title: 2023_PMC10229756_Adverse_Events_Following_Immunization_Among_Children_Under_Two_
ehr_evidence: Data was collected using a pretested, semi-structured questionnaire that contained 20 questions regarding the socio-demographic characteristics of the participants, vaccination details, and the AEFI history of the child; follow-up home visits on the 8th and 30th day of vaccination were carried out to identify occurrences of AEFIs.
summary: A prospective community-based observational study of 255 children under two years of age receiving vaccines under the Universal Immunization Program in North India that assessed the incidence and pattern of adverse events following immunization.
key_findings: The incidence of AEFI was 33.0 per 100 doses of vaccines administered, with 212 AEFIs reported from 152 of 255 vaccinated subjects.
Fever was the most common AEFI (101, 47.6%), followed by swelling at the injection site (53, 25.0%).
Pentavalent + OPV (48.8 per 100 doses) was majorly responsible for AEFIs, followed by DPT + MR + OPV (46.6 per 100 doses).
No significant association of AEFI with age and gender (p > 0.05).
All AEFIs were minor and no serious AEFIs were identified.
data_source_type: questionnaire/interview (primary data collection with follow-up home visits)
population: 255 children under two years of age receiving vaccines under the Universal Immunization Program in Haldwani block, Nainital district, Uttarakhand, North India
exposure_domain: Vaccination/immunization (vaccines under the Universal Immunization Program)
limitations: Single-block study limits generalization of findings.
Recall bias as AEFI identification was based on maternal history.
Could not attribute AEFIs to specific vaccines due to co-administration of multiple vaccines.
Small sample size with loss to follow-up contributing to potential selection bias.
